_comment: The repository settings THIS repository is expected to have.
Applied by the standards repository's scripts/apply-settings.sh, which
reads before it writes and previews by default. Every value here is
required by something documented: the reason is on the line beside it,
and a setting nothing needs is not here.
RUN BY HAND, NEVER FROM A WORKFLOW. Repository settings need a token with
administration write, which the default GITHUB_TOKEN is not and cannot be
made into. Running it by hand is what keeps that credential out of this
repository entirely, and this is the repository that holds the release
capability for six other trees.
SETTINGS ONLY. Branch and tag protection live in data/rulesets/ and are
applied separately, because they are the change that can lock you out.
Three endpoint groups, one plan: the repository block is the repository
object, the actions block is the Actions policy under Settings -> Actions
-> General (workflow token and fork pull requests), and the security block
has endpoints of its own.
Everything writable that is deliberately NOT here is in _excluded, with
the reason: absence is always a decision, never an oversight.
Some settings are gated on repository visibility or plan. Secret scanning
is free on public repositories and needs Advanced Security on private
ones, and private vulnerability reporting is a public-repository feature.
The script detects both and skips with a notice rather than failing.

_why.allow_squash_merge: Squash is the only door. Dependabot is the only pull-request author this repository expects, and a squashed update lands as one Conventional Commit subject instead of a vendor's own history.
_why.allow_merge_commit: A merge commit has no Conventional Commit subject, so the release notes generator cannot see it. Release notes are the only changelog this repository will have.
_why.allow_rebase_merge: Rebase replays commits individually, which puts unsquashed work-in-progress subjects on the branch that publishes to six other repositories.
_why.squash_merge_commit_title: The pull request title becomes the commit that lands, which is the subject the local commit-msg hook was written to shape.
_why.squash_merge_commit_message: The pull request body becomes the commit body, which is how a required body arrives without retyping it.
_why.delete_branch_on_merge: Nothing else prunes a merged Dependabot head, and this repository has exactly one long-lived branch by design.
_why.allow_auto_merge: Dependabot's pull requests are the only ones here, and every action they bump executes inside six other repositories' CI. Auto-merge lets a green update land without waiting on a human who would only have clicked the same button.
_why.allow_update_branch: Lets a pull request take the base branch without a merge commit, so a stale Dependabot branch can be refreshed in place.
_why.web_commit_signoff_required: Every commit that lands here is a human push or a release-workflow commit; this makes an edit made in the browser comply instead of failing. IT DOES NOT REACH THE PUBLISHING PATH, and that is why it is safe to turn on: the setting governs commits authored through the web UI and the API, and both the release bake commit and the sync commit are ordinary git pushes from a runner. Had the transport stayed on the GraphQL commit API this setting could have broken releases with an error naming the wrong cause.
_why.has_issues: ON HERE, UNLIKE THE PROVEN PUBLISHER IT COPIES. This repository is the fleet's issue intake by design: five of six consuming repositories have Issues disabled, and a consumer whose sync fails at startup cannot report anything from inside itself anyway. The intake has to live where the code that failed lives.
_why.has_discussions: Nothing routes here. The account-wide chooser is served from the public tannergolden/.github repository, and a second, near-empty forum in a single-maintainer publisher splits an audience of one.
_why.has_wiki: Documentation is versioned in the tree and reviewed. A wiki is neither, and this repository publishes documentation for a living.
_why.has_projects: Off by default rather than opinionated: turn it on deliberately if you use it.

_why_actions.default_workflow_permissions: This is the setting whose absence has no error log. It caps every job's declared permissions, so on read-only the release workflow's contents: write is silently narrowed and the run fails at STARTUP: no job, no step, nothing in the Actions tab to read. Leave it on Read and write and let each workflow narrow itself, which they all do.
_why_actions.can_approve_pull_request_reviews: Stated rather than left implicit. No workflow here approves a pull request today, but the endpoint is written as a whole: an unstated value is a value that drifts the next time the other key in this block changes.
_why_actions.fork_pr_approval_policy: This repository is public, so anyone can fork it, and its workflows are the ones that publish to six trees. A first-time contributor's fork workflows wait for a maintainer. PUBLIC repositories only: GitHub refuses the endpoint on a private repository, which an outsider cannot fork, so the run skips it with a notice.

_why_security.secret_scanning: The platform-native layer beside Gitleaks. Free here because the repository is public.
_why_security.secret_scanning_push_protection: Stops a credential at the boundary rather than reporting it afterwards. This repository is the one whose secrets would reach other people's runners.
_why_security.secret_scanning_non_provider_patterns: Widens platform scanning past provider tokens to generic credentials (private keys, connection strings), the same class Gitleaks hunts from the other side. Plan-gated: written only where the repository reports the feature.
_why_security.vulnerability_alerts: Dependabot alerts. The pinned third-party actions here execute inside every consumer's CI, so they must not rot quietly.
_why_security.automated_security_fixes: Dependabot security updates, which is what opens the pull requests that auto-merge then lands.
_why_security.private_vulnerability_reporting: Gives the Security tab a Report a vulnerability entry. This repository publishes an executable hook into other people's trees; a stranger who finds something needs somewhere to say so that is not a public issue.

_excluded._comment: Every writable repository setting that is deliberately NOT here, so absence is always a decision and never an oversight. The complete map of the surface, including what generation sets and what has no API at all, is docs/operations/Repository-Settings.md in the standards repository.
_excluded.name, description, homepage, topics: Identity. What this repository is called and about is set once, by hand, by a person; a shared value would overwrite it on every run.
_excluded.private / visibility: Changing who can see a repository is a human act with legal and billing consequences, never a side effect of a settings sync. This one is public on purpose: its output is copied into other people's trees and must be readable there.
_excluded.archived, is_template, default_branch: Structural state. Development is the default branch and means trunk here, not a stage; archiving and templating are one-time decisions.
_excluded.advanced_security / code_security: Paid per-committer on private repositories. Billing decisions belong to a person.
_excluded.secret_scanning_ai_detection: Copilot secret scanning is plan-gated and still moving; turn it on by hand where your plan has it.
_excluded.merge_commit_title, merge_commit_message: They configure a door this file nails shut: allow_merge_commit is false, so no one could ever see these values.
_excluded.allow_forking: Exists only on organization-owned repositories; personal public repositories are always forkable.
_excluded.immutable_releases: Deliberately deferred, not forgotten. It is free and permanent, and a release object accidentally attached to the bare v1 tag would lock that tag forever, which kills distribution and the only emergency brake at once. Turn it on by hand AFTER v1.0.0 publishes cleanly.
_excluded.required_signatures: Off, and it must stay off while the transport is a git push. A commit pushed from a runner with the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN is not signed and is not Verified, so requiring signatures would reject this repository's own release bake commit and every consumer's sync commit, with an error that names the signature rather than the design. Buying it back means a signing key in repository secrets, readable by anything that can run here, which is a larger loss than the gain.
_excluded.actions enabled / allowed_actions allowl: Actions is tautologically on. An action allowlist is real hardening with a real maintenance bill, and every third-party action here is already pinned to a full commit SHA, which an allowlist does not improve on.
_excluded.actions workflow access_level: Governs private repositories sharing workflows outward; this repository is public and shares them by being public.
_excluded.environments, pages, webhooks, autolinks: Project-specific wiring with no standard value. This repository has one maintainer and no deployments.
_excluded.interaction_limits: Temporary moderation levers by design; a sync that re-applied them would turn an incident response into permanent policy.
